I figure this could be a useful data point for people who are more into fitness than purely focused on running and thought I'd share my results and experience with taking a pretty long break from running. I was expecting to be much slower and in a lot more pain after taking such a long break.

Some stats and background: 30 year old male, regular running experience 2 years. I started 2014 off seriously getting into running and moderately into weight training, just coming off my first half marathon in October 2013. The first 5 months of 2014 I kept up with weight training but focused on training for a half marathon.

Shortly after that half, I had my sights set on my first full marathon in November. Just a few weeks before the marathon, I ran a half, because why not, and no surprise, it was to be my PR half, I ran 1:28:42 (6:47 min / mi pace). Now, as another point of information, I ran the marathon in 3:26:38 with ridiculously windy conditions.

After the marathon I wanted to focus on wight training, trying to gain muscle and bulk up over the winter. I had been weight training 3 - 4 times a week while marathon training and I had been looking forward to cutting the running out to see how my strength would improve, but felt I couldn't eat enough to keep up running while trying to bulk up. I ended up doing absolutely no running for nearly four months. Another point, I was doing Ice Cream Fitness, no cardio.

Since it had been a cold, snowy winter and I hate running outside below freezing and can't manage more than 5 miles on the treadmill I did very little training before my last half marathon last weekend.

As for training, I started with a couple treadmill 4 - 5 milers per week, three weeks from the marathon and got in a couple 6 mile runs outside and one 9 mile run the week before, so pretty minimal training. I ended up running, what I consider, a respectable 1:35:18 half (7:17 min / mi). Also, I was really not pushing myself hard, as it was my first race of the year and wanted to take it easy.

TL;DR Ran a half last October in 1:28:42, a marathon in November in 3:26:38, did zero running for nearly four months, lightly trained for 3 weeks and ran a 1:35:18 half.
